approach: Give the reader the missing information first, then widen the existing phrase check slightly. (1) In `verifier_can_run_section` (crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs:618-632) add one passage. It says the verifier sees only the final candidate tree, the diff and the recorded check output, and cannot check out or run anything on the base commit. A before/after comparison or "fails without the fix" criterion is met only by the diff or by a recorded Athena revert-run check, never by the verifier's own base run. The same section adds transcript and log to the producer-account nouns. (2) In crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs add "transcript" and "log" to REPORT_NOUNS (line 7, array length 5 to 7), so the existing loop at lines 57-64 builds the six phrase shapes for each. The doc comment of `producer_evidence_phrase` (line 47) names the root cause (no defined list of verifier-observable evidence), and the refusal message at lines 107-111 lists the new nouns. (3) Add one brief test in briefs.rs and one reading test in reading.rs. (4) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased / Changed naming the root cause and the expected 1% share. No new refusal machinery, record, config key or base-tree-run code. The information fix is primary. The noun extension is a small widening of an existing rule. Criterion 4 (fmt, clippy, test) is shown by running the three Athena checks against the final tree. That demonstration now names its seam and what fails without the change.

decisions.choice: Put the final-tree-only statement in the existing 'What the verifier can run' section of the reader brief, and name the recorded Athena revert-run check as the only way a 'fails without the fix' criterion is met besides the diff.
decisions.reason: The failing stage (the reader) lacked the list of what the verifier can observe. The section already lists the commands and says the verifier sees the diff, snapshot and check output (reader.rs:622-625). It never says base runs are impossible, so readers wrote criteria that asked for base-vs-candidate runs. Revert-run checks already exist as recorded checks (`CheckRun.revert_for`, used in reading/retry.rs:678 and run/close.rs:669), so naming them gives the reader a legal alternative.

rejected.option: A new refusal rule that scans criteria for 'base commit', 'before the change' or 'without the fix' wording
rejected.why: That wording is legitimate when it points at the diff or a revert-run check. Criterion 3 of this very reading uses 'fails on the base tree'. A scan would refuse valid readings, and the information fix prevents the failure without refusing anything.

rejected.option: Build revert-run or base-tree-run machinery for the verifier
rejected.why: Out of scope in the brief. Revert-run records already exist.

rejected.option: Edit the reader frame prompt file
rejected.why: Out of scope: it has 2 tokens of headroom (docs/system-facts.md: budget reader 1998 of 2000). The brief section is Rust string text outside the budgeted sets.

decisions.choice: Extend REPORT_NOUNS with 'transcript' and 'log' rather than adding new phrase families.
decisions.reason: Every noun gets the six existing phrase shapes (producer's X, producers' X, producer X, X from/of/by the producer) in the loop at surveys.rs:57-64, so one array edit covers the transcript and log forms. `has_phrase` requires whole words (surveys.rs:39-45), so 'producer's login expired' does not match 'producer's log'. A search of the whole snapshot (case-insensitive, regex for producer's/producer transcript or log, and transcript/log of/from/by the producer) found no existing text citing a producer log or transcript. In the refusal corpus, the only 'log' hits are 'git log' (refusal_corpus.rs:436, 441, 447), which no phrase matches.

rejected.why: REPORT_VERBS applies only to 'the report <verb>' (surveys.rs:69-71). The transcript noun belongs with the producer's own account nouns.

decisions.choice: Do not add a refusal_corpus case. The input form 'producer-report-evidence' is already mapped to case 'criterion-rests-on-the-producer-report'.
decisions.reason: The case (refusal_corpus.rs:1995-2005: tags dash-bullet and producer-report-evidence, text '- The producer's report lists the caller-check Grep', Expected::Refuse("check_criteria_evidence")) already carries the form. A transcript or log phrase is the same form, covered by the unit test in reading.rs. refusal_corpus.rs is not a listed deliverable. The corpus run is a demonstration so that the existing case is guarded against regression.

rejected.option: Add a second corpus case for a transcript criterion
rejected.why: It would edit a file outside the deliverable list for a form the corpus already covers.

decisions.choice: Show criterion 4 by running the three Athena checks on the final tree, and name the production commands themselves as the seam.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 is a behavior criterion about the final tree passing the checks Athena records. The seam is the checks' own commands, with the working tree as the fixture. Nothing is doubled, so no logic under test sits in a fake. The checks are those listed in the brief: fmt `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, test `cargo test --locked`.

rejected.option: Replace the criterion 4 demonstration with a reading of the recorded check output alone
rejected.why: The verifier can run these commands itself, which is stronger than reading a record. The recorded checks are named as a second observation.

risks.risk: 'log' as a noun could refuse a legitimate criterion such as 'the producer log file is not committed'.
risks.mitigation: Matching is whole-word and only in phrases that tie the noun to the producer (producer's log, producer log, log of/from/by the producer; surveys.rs:39-45, 57-64). A search of the snapshot found no existing criterion or corpus case with that wording. The stated estimate is 1% of newly refused readings, an estimate from the reading and not measured here. The refusal message tells the reader how to restate the criterion.

risks.risk: The brief wording promises a 'recorded Athena revert-run check', which exists only for jobs where Athena records one.
risks.mitigation: The text says 'by the diff or by a recorded Athena revert-run check'. The existing revert-run records (`CheckRun.revert_for`, reading/retry.rs:678, run/close.rs:669) are not changed, and the reader may still use the diff.

risks.risk: A longer reader brief section could break a brief-size or ordering test.
risks.mitigation: I found only the ordering test at briefs.rs:4075 (heading precedes the section) and no size cap on the reader brief. `cargo test --locked` runs the whole suite, including athena-context.

risks.risk: A rustfmt or clippy failure on the long string literals or the changed array length would fail criterion 4 after an otherwise correct change.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 runs `cargo fmt --all` then the three checks on the final tree. The array length is changed together with the two new entries so it compiles.

demonstrations.method: Run the new brief test. It builds the reader brief through the production renderer and checks the 'What the verifier can run' section text.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The section contains 'only the final candidate tree', 'base commit', 'before/after' and 'revert-run', and still contains 'never the producer's report' and 'is refused'. The older test the_reader_brief_says_the_verifier_never_sees_the_producers_report (briefs.rs:4045-4051) keeps passing.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the section has no final-tree-only or base-commit wording (reader.rs:622-625), so the new test's assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `reader_brief(&ReaderInputs)` (reader.rs:380 calls `verifier_can_run_section`, reader.rs:618). Guard: the section is left out when `verifier_can_run` is empty (reader.rs:619). The fixture `reader_inputs(&reading())` (briefs.rs:3717) sets `verifier_can_run: vec![("change", ["cargo test"])]` (briefs.rs:3729), so the section is rendered. The new test is added in step 3 and uses the same fixture as the existing test at briefs.rs:4045. The seam exists. The real renderer is called and nothing is doubled.

Grep of surveys.rs finds 'transcript' and 'log' in REPORT_NOUNS (line 7) and the root-cause wording ('no defined list') in the doc comment above `producer_evidence_phrase` (line 47).

Fixtures `reader_inputs(&reading())` (briefs.rs:3717) and `reading_with_criterion` (reading.rs:4539) exist today. The corpus runs the refusal through the production `Expected::Refuse("check_criteria_evidence")` path of refusal_corpus.rs. No double carries logic under test.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks on the final working tree, one command each, and compare with the recorded check output for the final tree. The observation is that all three exit 0. This command is the fmt check. The other two are `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.
demonstrations.observes: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` each exit 0, with no formatting diff, no clippy warning and no failing test. Athena's recorded checks on the final tree (fmt, clippy, test) show the same.
demonstrations.fails_without: A candidate that left the change unfinished would fail one of the commands. A long writeln! line left unformatted in reader.rs makes fmt print a diff. A REPORT_NOUNS array whose declared length (`[&str; 7]`) does not match its seven entries is a compile error, which fails clippy and test. An unused binding or needless clone in the new tests triggers a `-D warnings` clippy error. An edit that drops 'never the producer's report' or 'is refused' from the section would fail the existing test at briefs.rs:4045-4051. Dropping a word from the refusal text that reading.rs:4557-4561 asserts would fail the existing reading test at 4550-4562.
demonstrations.seam: The production commands are the entry points: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, as listed under 'Checks Athena will run on the result'. The fixture is the final candidate tree (the repository snapshot with the producer's edits), and no test double is used. The recorded check output is read with `git show` or the job's check records. The seam exists, since the checks are Athena's own configured commands and run on any tree. Step 6 runs them on the final tree.
